introduction: Tailored for UGC NET and advanced DSSSB/KVS exams, this level dissects the clinical changes in the DSM-5, the neurological brain structures affected in SLDs, and the legislative mandates of the RPwD Act 2016 regarding benchmarking and certification.

core_concepts.title: DSM-5 Changes in Autism & SLD
core_concepts.description:
The American Psychiatric Association's DSM-5 (2013) brought massive changes to diagnostic criteria:
1. Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD): In older manuals (DSM-IV), Asperger's Syndrome, PDD-NOS, and Autistic Disorder were separate diagnoses. DSM-5 merged them all into a single umbrella diagnosis called **ASD**. (Asperger's is no longer an official clinical diagnosis; it is now considered 'Level 1 ASD' or high-functioning autism).
2. Specific Learning Disorder: DSM-5 eliminated the standalone diagnoses of Dyslexia and Dyscalculia. Instead, it uses one overarching category: 'Specific Learning Disorder', with specific specifiers (e.g., 'Specific Learning Disorder with impairment in reading').

core_concepts.title: Neurobiology of Dyslexia and ADHD
core_concepts.description:
- Dyslexia: fMRI scans show underactivity in the left hemisphere's posterior reading systems (Parieto-temporal area for word analysis and Occipito-temporal area for rapid word form recognition). Dyslexic brains often over-rely on the right hemisphere and frontal lobe (Broca's area) to compensate.
- ADHD: Linked to delayed maturation and reduced volume in the **Prefrontal Cortex** (responsible for executive functions) and the **Basal Ganglia**. It involves dysregulation of neurotransmitters, specifically Dopamine and Norepinephrine.

core_concepts.title: Co-morbidity
core_concepts.description:
The simultaneous presence of two or more independent conditions in a patient. Neurodevelopmental disorders are highly co-morbid. 
For example, approximately 30% to 50% of children with ADHD also have a co-occurring Specific Learning Disability (like Dyslexia). A child can have ASD, ADHD, and Dyspraxia simultaneously. Teachers must create an Individualized Education Program (IEP) that addresses the overlapping complexities.

core_concepts.title: RPwD Act 2016: Certification and Benchmarking
core_concepts.description:
The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 officially recognized 'Specific Learning Disabilities' and 'Autism Spectrum Disorder' as legal disabilities for the first time in Indian law.
- Benchmark Disability: A person must have at least **40%** of the specified disability, certified by a medical board, to avail of government benefits, including 5% reservation in higher education and 4% in government jobs.
- Inclusive Mandate: The act strictly mandates that educational institutions cannot deny admission based on SLD/ASD and must provide 'reasonable accommodation'.

important_entities.name: Orton-Gillingham (OG) Approach
important_entities.key_fact: The gold standard instructional approach for Dyslexia.
important_entities.significance: Developed in the 1930s, it breaks reading and spelling down into smaller skills involving letters and sounds, and then builds on these skills over time. It is heavily **Multisensory** (incorporating visual, auditory, and kinesthetic/tactile pathways simultaneously to imprint learning into the brain).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a modern (post-2013 framework) UGC NET question asks 'Which of the following is an independent diagnosis in the DSM-5?', do NOT choose Asperger's Syndrome. It has been subsumed into the broader 'Autism Spectrum Disorder' category.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember that Dyslexia represents a dysfunction primarily in the **Left Hemisphere** of the brain (Parieto-temporal and Occipito-temporal regions), forcing the brain to compensate using the front and right sides.

exam_strategy_tips: When a question asks about the legal rights of a child with Dyslexia in India, reference the **RPwD Act 2016**. Remember that the previous PwD Act 1995 only covered 7 disabilities and did NOT legally cover SLDs or Autism.
